title: AI's Next Big Leap? General Intuition Grabs $320M to Pioneer 'Action' Models
summary: General Intuition, a new AI startup, has secured $320 million in funding from prominent investors like Khosla Ventures and Jeff Bezos. The company aims to develop "large action foundation models" that allow AI to understand, reason, and act within dynamic environments, distinguishing itself from conventional language models.
content:
Silicon Valley's insatiable appetite for artificial intelligence continues unabated, and the latest beneficiary is General Intuition, a stealthy startup that just closed a massive $320 million funding round. Led by the ever-prescient Khosla Ventures, the Series A also saw significant participation from an all-star roster including General Catalyst, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, and Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. This substantial capital infusion signals immense confidence in a company poised to push AI's boundaries well beyond the conversational models currently dominating headlines.

General Intuition isn't chasing the generative AI language model gold rush. Instead, it boldly describes itself as a "frontier lab for acting in space and time." This isn't about crafting eloquent prose or generating photorealistic images; it's about building "large action foundation models." Unlike traditional large language models (LLMs) that predict the next word, General Intuition's ambition is to develop AI that can understand, reason, and *act* within dynamic physical or simulated environments, truly interacting with the world.

Imagine AI agents capable of intricate problem-solving, navigating complex robotic tasks, or executing multi-step operations in real-world scenarios – not just processing information, but influencing it. This shift from language comprehension to direct action marks a profound pivot in AI development, aiming to bridge the gap between digital intelligence and practical, real-world utility. Such capabilities could unlock unprecedented levels of automation and intelligent system design across industries.

With this substantial war chest and the backing of some of tech's most influential figures, General Intuition is now exceptionally well-positioned to pioneer this next wave of AI. Their focus on models that act rather than merely articulate suggests a future where AI isn't just a powerful tool for information, but an intelligent agent actively shaping and responding to the physical world around us. The coming years will reveal just how far these "action models" can stretch the imagination.
keyTakeaways: General Intuition raised $320 million in a funding round led by Khosla Ventures, with participation from Jeff Bezos, Eric Schmidt, and General Catalyst.
The startup focuses on "large action foundation models" designed for AI to act and interact in physical or simulated environments.
This approach represents a significant departure from traditional large language models (LLMs), aiming for practical, real-world utility beyond text generation.
author: ETtech

title: Empowering Communities: FirstBank Fuels Imo State's Vision for Grassroots Prosperity
summary: FirstBank has thrown its considerable financial muscle behind Imo State's 'One Kindred One Business Initiative' (OKOBI), a groundbreaking community-based program. This initiative is designed to ignite job creation, expand financial inclusion, and cultivate sustainable entrepreneurship across the state.
content:
In a nation grappling with persistent unemployment and the urgent need for economic diversification, a significant partnership is blossoming in Imo State, Nigeria. FirstBank, a titan in the country's banking sector, is providing crucial backing to the Imo State Government's 'One Kindred One Business Initiative' (ÓKÓBÌ), a visionary program poised to transform local economies from the ground up.

ÓKÓBÌ isn't just another government scheme; it's a meticulously designed, community-based entrepreneurship program with a clear mandate. Its core objectives are multi-faceted: to stimulate job creation by empowering local ventures, expand the reach of financial inclusion to previously underserved populations, and foster sustainable business practices within the heart of Imo's communities. The genius lies in its reliance on the existing social fabric – the 'kindred' – to identify and nurture entrepreneurial talent, ensuring that support is tailored and impactful.

FirstBank's involvement elevates this initiative from a promising idea to a robust platform for change. Their support isn't merely symbolic; it represents a significant injection of resources, expertise, and credibility that will be vital in translating ÓKÓBÌ's ambitious goals into tangible results. This partnership underscores FirstBank's broader commitment to nation-building, demonstrating a proactive approach to social investment that goes beyond traditional banking services, aiming instead to cultivate an ecosystem of growth and self-sufficiency at the grassroots level.

Looking beyond the immediate impact in Imo State, the ÓKÓBÌ initiative, bolstered by FirstBank, could serve as a powerful blueprint for other Nigerian states and even regions across Africa. By leveraging community structures and combining government vision with private-sector financial might, it offers a compelling model for sustainable economic development and a pathway to widespread prosperity. It's a testament to the power of collaboration in unlocking human potential and building resilient local economies.
keyTakeaways: FirstBank is a major financial backer of Imo State's 'One Kindred One Business Initiative' (ÓKÓBÌ).
ÓKÓBÌ is a community-based program focused on stimulating job creation and expanding financial inclusion.
The initiative aims to foster sustainable entrepreneurship and offers a potential model for grassroots economic development.
author: Urowayino Jeremiah

title: OpenAI Fires Up the AI Chip Wars with Custom 'Jalapeño' Processor
summary: OpenAI has unveiled "Jalapeño," its first custom AI chip designed for inference, developed in just nine months with partners Broadcom and Celestica. This strategic move signals OpenAI's deep dive into hardware development, aiming to optimize performance, cut costs, and secure its supply chain in the escalating AI race.
content:
OpenAI, the powerhouse behind ChatGPT, just threw a spicy new ingredient into the simmering AI hardware pot: "Jalapeño." This custom-designed AI chip, unveiled on Wednesday, marks the startup’s ambitious foray into building its own silicon, specifically tailored for inference – the critical process that allows AI models to deliver their real-world magic. Developed at a blistering pace in just nine months, Jalapeño is more than just a piece of silicon; it's a clear strategic statement from Sam Altman's company.

The move isn't born of whim, but necessity. As AI models grow exponentially in complexity, so does the demand for specialized computing power. Relying solely on off-the-shelf solutions, particularly from dominant players like Nvidia, becomes an increasingly expensive and potentially bottleneck-ridden proposition. By crafting its own inference chip, OpenAI aims to optimize performance precisely for its own cutting-edge models, drastically reduce operational costs, and secure a more independent and resilient supply chain for its future innovations.

This monumental engineering feat wasn't a solo act. OpenAI shrewdly partnered with industry titans to bring Jalapeño to life. Broadcom took the reins on the intricate silicon implementation, networking, and vital connectivity aspects, leveraging their deep expertise. Meanwhile, Celestica stepped in to craft the physical computing hardware, including the circuit board, the robust hardware frame, and the overarching system architecture, translating the digital design into a tangible, functional piece of technology.

Jalapeño’s arrival signals a significant shift in the AI landscape, echoing moves by other tech giants like Google and Amazon who have long pursued custom silicon. For OpenAI, it represents a bold step towards vertical integration, granting them unprecedented control over their infrastructure stack. This isn't merely about faster computation; it's about shaping the very future of AI development from the ground up, ensuring that as their models evolve, their hardware can keep pace without compromise. The AI chip war just got a whole lot hotter.
keyTakeaways: OpenAI launched "Jalapeño," its first custom AI chip, designed for inference and built in a rapid nine months.
The strategic move aims to optimize AI model performance, reduce operational costs, and secure OpenAI's hardware supply chain.
OpenAI collaborated with Broadcom for silicon implementation and networking, and Celestica for the physical computing hardware.
author: ETtech
